request.spec:
A person's name must be unique on the sheet, comparing without regard to case and ignoring
spaces before and after the name. Names are stored with those surrounding spaces removed and
shown that way. Adding or editing a person to a name already in use is refused with an error on
the form, and nothing is saved.

agent.result_text:
Person names are now unique on each sheet, ignoring case and spaces before and after, and `bin/e2e` passes.

- **Server:** names are stored and shown without the surrounding spaces. Adding a person, or renaming one, to a name already on the sheet is refused with HTTP 409 and nothing is saved. Renaming a person to their own name in different case (for example "ben" to "Ben") is still allowed.
- **Stored data:** a new migration, `V4__person_name_unique.sql`, removes surrounding spaces from existing names. It also adds a lower-cased copy of the name with a unique index per sheet. That index also stops two users from saving the same name at the same moment; the app reports that clash as the same refusal.
- **Front end:** the form shows "That name is already in use." in `person-form-error`. A refused edit leaves the editor open.

The change is in `PersonService.java`, `PersonRepository.java`, the new `PersonNameTakenException.java`, and `core/people.ts`. The migration would fail if a sheet already held two names that differ only in case or spaces. That can't happen here, because the database is in-memory and starts empty on every run.
